findings.title: Sensitive user data stored in browser localStorage without encryption
findings.description: User credentials and profile information (user_id, user_role, user_name, user_email) are stored in plain text in localStorage. This violates secure token storage practices and exposes sensitive data to XSS attacks and malicious scripts.

locations.snippet:
localStorage.setItem('user_id', data.session.user.id)
localStorage.setItem('user_role', profile!.role)
localStorage.setItem('user_name', profile!.name)
localStorage.setItem('user_email', profile!.email)

public name: string = localStorage.getItem('user_name') || ''
email: string = localStorage.getItem('user_email') || ''
id: string = localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ''
created_by: localStorage.getItem('user_id') || ""

findings.suggested_fix: Replace localStorage with Supabase session management. Use Supabase's built-in session handling which stores tokens in secure, HTTP-only cookies. Remove all manual localStorage.setItem() calls and instead retrieve user data from Supabase's getSession() or getUser() methods. Store only non-sensitive identifiers if needed, and never store role/email in localStorage. Example: const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession(); // Use session.user directly instead of localStorage

findings.title: Missing token refresh mechanism and session expiration validation
findings.description: The application uses Supabase JWT tokens but does not implement automatic token refresh or validate token expiration before making API calls. Expired tokens will silently fail, causing poor UX and potential security gaps where stale sessions remain active.

locations.snippet: // File exists but full implementation not shown - need to verify token refresh logic

findings.suggested_fix: Implement token refresh in the Supabase service. Add a method to refresh the session before expiration: async refreshSessionIfNeeded() { const { data: { session } } = await this.supabase.auth.getSession(); if (session && this.isTokenExpiringSoon(session)) { await this.supabase.auth.refreshSession(); } }. Call this method in authGuard before checking user permissions. Consider using Supabase's built-in onAuthStateChange() to automatically handle token refresh events.

findings.title: Insufficient role-based access control in auth guard
findings.description: The authGuard checks if roles array exists and has length > 0, but requires roles to be explicitly defined in route data. Routes without defined roles default to denying access (returning false), but this creates an error state rather than graceful handling. More critically, there's no validation that profile.role actually matches UserRole enum values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add enum validation and fix the guard logic: (1) Validate that profile.role is a valid UserRole enum value before casting: if (!Object.values(UserRole).includes(profile.role)) { await supabase.signOut(); router.navigate(['/login']); return false; } (2) For routes without roles defined, should either deny with error logging or allow publicly. Current implicit deny is confusing. (3) Add logging when role mismatch occurs for audit purposes: console.warn(`Unauthorized access attempt: user ${user.id} with role ${profile.role} tried to access ${route.data['roles']}`);

findings.title: No CSRF protection on form submissions
findings.description: The login form and other POST operations (product creation, mismatch resolution) use HTTP methods without visible CSRF token validation. While Supabase may provide backend protection, frontend-level CSRF tokens are not implemented or validated.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection using Angular's built-in HttpClientXsrfModule. In app.config.ts, add: provideHttpClientXsrfProtection() and configure the token header/param names. Ensure all POST/PUT/DELETE requests include the X-XSRF-TOKEN header. This is typically handled automatically by Angular if properly configured in the HTTP interceptor. Verify Supabase client is using Angular HttpClient with XSRF interceptor enabled.

findings.title: Hardcoded role checks without centralized authorization service
findings.description: Role-based access is checked in multiple components using hardcoded string comparisons (e.g., 'admin', 'sales'). This scattered logic makes it difficult to audit and maintain authorization rules, and there's no centralized policy enforcement.

locations.snippet:
<!-- Admin Section -->
        <ng-container *ngIf="userRole === 'admin'">

findings.suggested_fix: Create a centralized authorization service: export class AuthorizationService { hasRole(requiredRole: UserRole): boolean { return this.getCurrentUserRole() === requiredRole; } canAccess(feature: string): boolean { const userRole = this.getCurrentUserRole(); const rolePermissions = { [UserRole.admin]: ['inventory', 'staff', 'products'], [UserRole.sales]: ['sales_dashboard'] }; return rolePermissions[userRole]?.includes(feature) || false; } } Inject this service into components instead of checking localStorage directly. Use it in templates as *ngIf="authService.hasRole(UserRole.admin)"

findings.title: No protection against account enumeration via login endpoint
findings.description: The login component shows detailed error messages that could allow attackers to enumerate valid user accounts (e.g., 'Login failed: User not found' vs 'Login failed: Invalid password').
findings.suggested_fix: Use generic error messages for login failures: if (error) { this.toast.show('Invalid email or password', 'error'); return; } Do not expose whether the email exists or if the password is wrong. Log detailed errors server-side only for debugging purposes. This prevents account enumeration attacks while maintaining good UX.

findings.title: Disabled user accounts not immediately revoked on login
findings.description: While the code checks if profile.is_active is false and signs out the user, it still allows them to proceed to role-based routing before the check happens. The check occurs after session creation, not as part of the authentication flow.
findings.suggested_fix: The logic is actually correct, but should be moved earlier or used in conjunction with Supabase RLS policies. Ensure database Row Level Security (RLS) policies on all sensitive tables enforce is_active = true. This way, even if a disabled user somehow gets past frontend checks, they cannot access data. Also consider: (1) calling getRLS-protected endpoints before showing dashboard, (2) implementing automatic logout if is_active becomes false during session (already done in app.component.ts with realtime subscription)

findings.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP) headers
findings.description: No Content Security Policy is defined in index.html or server configuration. This leaves the application vulnerable to XSS attacks and allows arbitrary script execution.

locations.snippet:

<html lang="en">

<head>

    <link rel="icon" type="image/x-icon" href="favicon.ico" />

findings.suggested_fix: Add CSP meta tag to index.html: <meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.jsdelivr.net https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src 'self' data: https:; connect-src 'self' https://*.supabase.co; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;">. Additionally, configure CSP in server headers (Nginx/Docker) for better enforcement. Review and restrict external CDN dependencies (Chart.js from CDN should ideally be bundled).

findings.title: Automatic logout service may not properly invalidate tokens
findings.description: The auto-logout.service is referenced but not shown in provided code. If it relies only on client-side timers without backend session invalidation, tokens could remain valid server-side even after logout.

locations.snippet: // File not provided - cannot verify implementation

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that auto-logout.service.ts properly calls supabase.auth.signOut() which invalidates the session server-side. Ensure: (1) Client-side timer triggers server-side logout, not just local cleanup. (2) All HTTP interceptors immediately clear authentication state upon 401 response. (3) Refresh tokens are also invalidated. If auto-logout is only client-side, add: await this.supabase.auth.signOut(); this.router.navigate(['/login']);

findings.title: Password visibility toggle exposes input value in DOM

findings.suggested_fix: This is an acceptable UX pattern, but mitigate risks by: (1) Ensuring password value is never logged or stored in memory longer than needed. findings.title: No explicit HTTP-only and Secure cookie configuration visible
findings.description: While Supabase handles session cookies internally, there's no evidence that the application is enforcing HTTP-only and Secure flags or validating cookie security policies.

locations.snippet:
import { ApplicationConfig, provideZoneChangeDetection } from '@angular/core'
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router'
import { provideHttpClient } from '@angular/common/http'

import { routes } from './app.routes'

export const appConfig: ApplicationConfig = {
    providers: [
        provideZoneChangeDetection({ eventCoalescing: true }),
        provideRouter(routes),
        provideHttpClient(),
    ],
}

findings.suggested_fix: Add HttpClientXsrfModule and ensure Supabase client is configured with secure defaults: provideHttpClientWithInterceptors([xsrfInterceptor]). In Supabase initialization, verify session storage is set to 'memory' not 'localStorage'. Configure app to require HTTPS in production. Add HTTP security headers in Nginx/Docker config: add_header Strict-Transport-Security 'max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains' always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options 'nosniff' always;

findings.title: No protection against brute force login attempts
findings.description: The login endpoint has no rate limiting, account lockout mechanism, or progressive delay. An attacker can attempt unlimited login tries without consequences.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement client-side rate limiting using a service: export class RateLimitService { private loginAttempts: { [email: string]: { count: number; timestamp: number } } = {}; canAttemptLogin(email: string): boolean { const key = email; const now = Date.now(); if (this.loginAttempts[key] && now - this.loginAttempts[key].timestamp < 900000) { if (this.loginAttempts[key].count >= 5) return false; } return true; } recordAttempt(email: string) { this.loginAttempts[email] = { count: (this.loginAttempts[email]?.count || 0) + 1, timestamp: Date.now() }; } }. Call canAttemptLogin() before handleLogin(). For server-side: use Supabase's built-in auth protection or implement fail2ban rules.

findings.title: Sensitive modal operations lack authorization checks
findings.description: The reconciliation modal that allows admins to void transactions and the product pricing modal allow sensitive operations without re-confirming authorization or checking permissions beyond initial route guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Add server-side authorization checks for sensitive operations: (1) Before calling supabase.resolveMismatch() or supabase.voidSale(), verify user role is admin by calling a protected endpoint. (2) Supabase RLS policies should enforce: CREATE POLICY "Only admins can resolve mismatches" ON mismatches FOR UPDATE USING (auth.jwt() ->> 'role' = 'admin'); (3) Require secondary confirmation using email verification or TOTP for financial transactions. (4) Implement audit logging for all sensitive operations on backend.

findings.title: Unvalidated product search input allowing potential XSS
findings.description: The products component accepts searchTerm from user input without sanitization and directly filters products based on string matching. While this doesn't directly render untrusted HTML, the pattern is vulnerable if search results are later displayed with interpolation in templates without property binding.

locations.snippet: search

findings.suggested_fix: Implement input sanitization and validation: (1) Add length limits to search input: `maxlength="100"`. (2) Use Angular's DomSanitizer if results must be rendered as HTML (unlikely here). (3) Validate searchTerm on input: `onSearch(event: any) { const value = (event.target.value || '').trim().slice(0, 100); if(/^[a-zA-Z0-9\s\-]*$/.test(value)) { this.searchTerm = value; this.filterProducts(); } }`. (4) Ensure template uses property binding: `{{ product.name }}` (already correct).

findings.title: Missing CSRF protection on state-changing operations
findings.description: The application uses Angular's default HTTP client setup without explicit CSRF token handling in headers. While Supabase handles auth via JWT, state-changing operations like void transactions, product deletion, and reconciliation updates do not include CSRF tokens. The code relies solely on authentication without additional CSRF protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement CSRF protection via HTTP headers: (1) Configure Angular's HttpClientXsrfModule in app.config.ts: `import { provideHttpClient, withXsrfConfiguration } from '@angular/common/http'; ...provideHttpClient(withXsrfConfiguration({ cookieName: 'XSRF-TOKEN', headerName: 'X-XSRF-TOKEN' }))`. (2) Ensure backend validates XSRF tokens on state-changing requests. (3) Alternative: Use SameSite=Strict cookies (server-side config) which mitigates CSRF without explicit tokens.

findings.title: Unvalidated object assignment in reconciliation resolution
findings.description: The reconciliation component uses ngModel for form binding without strict type validation. The manualQty field accepts any value from input and is used directly in calculation without type coercion validation. The resolutionNote field is also unvalidated and passed directly to backend.
findings.suggested_fix: Use reactive forms with validators: (1) Replace ngModel with FormGroup: `this.resolutionForm = this.fb.group({ manualQty: [0, [Validators.required, Validators.min(0), Validators.max(999999), Validators.pattern(/^[0-9]+$/)]], resolutionNote: ['', [Validators.maxLength(500)]] })`. (2) In template: `<input type="number" formControlName="manualQty" min="0" max="999999" step="1">`. (3) Validate before submission: `if (this.resolutionForm.invalid) { return; }`. (4) Sanitize note input: `note = note.trim().slice(0, 500);`

findings.title: Unencrypted sensitive data in API responses and state
findings.description: The application receives and stores sensitive financial data (transaction amounts, customer details, stock counts) in component state and displays them in the DOM without explicit encryption or protection. The data flows from Supabase (over HTTPS, which is good) but is stored in plaintext in memory and potentially in browser caches.

locations.snippet:
Total Revenue {{ financials.totalRevenue | currency:'NGN':'symbol-narrow' }}
💵 Cash at Hand {{ financials.cashAtHand | currency:'NGN':'symbol-narrow' }}

findings.suggested_fix: Implement data protection measures: (1) Use Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent DOM-based data exfiltration: `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self';`. (2) Set `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate` on responses containing financial data. (3) Add `pragma: no-cache` headers. (4) Clear sensitive state on logout: `this.financials = { totalRevenue: 0, ... }` in logout handler. (5) Consider using Angular's OnDestroy to clear sensitive arrays: `ngOnDestroy() { this.financials = null; }`

findings.title: Unvalidated receipt/invoice data passed to DOM without sanitization
findings.description: The reconciliation and analysis components display invoice data (item summaries, descriptions, product names) directly in templates using string interpolation. findings.title: Unvalidated numerical input in expense and stock calculations
findings.description: The analysis component calculates financial metrics (totalSpent, netProfit) from database values without validating that amounts are valid positive numbers. If backend data is corrupted or user manipulates data upstream, calculations could produce NaN or Infinity values.
findings.suggested_fix: Add numeric validation and bounds checking: (1) Validate each value: `const cost = typeof e.total_cost === 'number' && e.total_cost >= 0 ? e.total_cost : 0;`. (2) Add max value checks: `if (cost > 999999999) cost = 999999999;`. (3) After calculation, validate result: `this.expenseMetrics.netProfit = Math.max(-999999999, Math.min(999999999, this.financials.totalRevenue - total));`. (4) Add Number.isFinite() checks: `if (!Number.isFinite(total)) { total = 0; }`. (5) Example: `const cost = Math.max(0, Math.min(999999999, parseFloat(e.total_cost) || 0));`

findings.title: Hardcoded CDN URL for external scripts without integrity checks
findings.description: The application loads Chart.js from CDN without Subresource Integrity (SRI) verification. If the CDN is compromised or MITM attack occurs, malicious script could be loaded. Font Awesome and Google Fonts are also loaded from external sources without SRI.

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/font-awesome/4.7.0/css/font-awesome.min.css" />

findings.suggested_fix: Add Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes and verify remote sources: (1) For Chart.js, add integrity hash: `<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js@4.5.1" integrity="sha384-<HASH>" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>` (get hash from jsDelivr or npm). (3) For Google Fonts, add nonce or preload: `<link rel="preload" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?..." as="style">`. (4) Update CSP to require SRI: `script-src 'self' https: 'require-sri-for-script';`. (5) Prefer npm packages over CDN when possible.

findings.description: The Supabase service makes multiple API calls (authentication, data queries, realtime subscriptions) without apparent rate limiting. No throttling mechanism is visible in the SupabaseService, and Angular HttpClient is configured without rate limit interceptors. This exposes the application to brute-force attacks, DOS, and resource exhaustion.

findings.title: Missing request timeout configuration
findings.description: Angular HttpClient is configured without explicit timeout settings. Long-running requests or network hangs could leave connections open indefinitely, consuming resources and enabling slowloris-style DOS attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add HTTP timeout configuration with interceptor: (1) Create custom HTTP interceptor that adds timeout: `timeout(30000)` (30 seconds), (2) Apply to all HTTP calls: `provideHttpClient(withInterceptors([timeoutInterceptor]))`, (3) For critical API calls, use shorter timeouts. Example interceptor: `export function timeoutInterceptor(req: HttpRequest<any>, next: HttpHandlerFn) { return next(req).pipe(timeout(30000)); }` or use `req.clone()` with explicit settings. Consider different timeouts: file uploads (60s), normal API (30s), login (15s).
